archetype.name: Dual-Threat (pass-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback whose arm now drives the offense, throwing with rare accuracy at every depth, while his legs show up mostly as off-script scrambles that keep drives alive rather than as a heavy diet of designed runs.

report.headline: League-best passing efficiency built on soft defenses, now paused by an ankle sprain.
report.take:
Jackson has played four games, and on a per-throw basis he has been the best passer among the 43 qualifiers. He ranks first in yards per attempt (10.07), first in adjusted net yards per dropback (10.74) and first in CPOE (+8.3), and fourth in EPA per dropback (0.363). This is not a dink-and-dunk profile padded by completions. His intermediate throws (10-19 air yards) are returning 0.904 EPA, his deep balls 0.745, and he is pushing the ball 1.18 yards past the sticks on average. In a Baltimore offense that passes 6 points less than situation predicts (27th), he is being asked to be efficient, not prolific, and he has been.

The main driver is Zay Flowers. Flowers has 19 targets at 1.46 EPA per target, which is absurd. Bateman (0.644) and Mark Andrews (23 targets, 0.319) have been solid around him. The other driver is time: Jackson's 3.11-second time to throw is long, but Baltimore's line has allowed the second-lowest hit rate in the league. He is getting clean pockets, holding the ball and hitting throws downfield. The legs have changed shape. He has only six designed runs in four games. The rushing value now comes from ten scrambles worth 0.48 EPA each, six of which moved the chains. That continues a trend from 2025, when his 349 rushing yards ranked just 12th after years of leading the position.

The opponents are the big caveat. Indianapolis, New Orleans, Dallas and Tennessee currently rank 26th, 27th, 32nd and 25th in defensive EPA. All four are bottom-eight units, and the one that blitzed him heavily (New Orleans, 15 blitzes) produced his only sub-10 passing-EPA game and his only interception. Some underlying charting also reads less clean than the CPOE. His bad-throw rate of 16.7% ranks 33rd of 36. His third-down success rate is 34.8%. His red-zone EPA is slightly negative even with four touchdowns. Some of that is noise on tiny samples, and the third-down number comes with an average of 9.2 yards to go. Still, it argues that a 10-yards-per-attempt pace against soft defenses is partly the schedule.

The immediate question is the left ankle. He played only 52% of snaps in Week 4, sat Week 5 while Tyler Huntley started, and is listed Out with a projected return on the date of the Cleveland game. The coach says he is "definitely doing better." When he returns, expect a very good quarterback, not one throwing for 10 yards an attempt. The bigger risk is that a sprained ankle trims the scrambling that has quietly been a real piece of his value.

strengths.title: Accuracy at every depth
strengths.body: He leads qualifiers in CPOE and is completing throws over expectation short, intermediate and deep, with the intermediate window especially lethal. His career CPOE has bounced between roughly -0.6 and +4.6 since 2019, so +8.3 is a peak, not his norm. Expect it to settle, probably still well above average.

strengths.title: Vertical game with Flowers
strengths.body: Flowers is producing 1.46 EPA per target, and the deep ball overall is returning 0.745 EPA despite a 44% completion rate. That is the right trade for a downfield passer: misses are cheap, hits are huge. The per-target figure will regress hard on 19 targets, but the connection is the engine of this passing game.

strengths.title: Scrambles as a drive-saver
strengths.body: Ten scrambles have produced 107 yards and six first downs at 0.48 EPA apiece, which more than pays for his long time to throw. This is the part of the profile most exposed to the ankle injury.

concerns.title: Ankle sprain clouds availability
concerns.body: He is listed Out, missed Week 5, and played only half the snaps in Week 4. The projected return lands on game day, which is an estimate, not a commitment. Even if he plays, a mobility-limited Jackson loses the scramble value that rescues broken plays.

concerns.title: Production came against weak defenses
concerns.body: Every opponent so far ranks 25th or worse in defensive EPA. The game where he faced the heaviest blitz load produced his lowest passing EPA and his only interception. The efficiency ranks are real but schedule-inflated.

concerns.title: Charting and money downs lag
concerns.body: A bottom-tier bad-throw rate and a 34.8% third-down success rate sit awkwardly beside a league-best CPOE. Some of that comes from long yardage (9.2 to go). Bad-throw rates in the bottom half have followed him his whole career, so this is partly who he is rather than noise.

trend.note: Outside a blitz-heavy Week 2 loss to New Orleans (3.3 passing EPA), he posted 10-12 passing EPA in every game, including a Week 4 he did not finish. The ankle has paused the run, so the next data point is about health as much as form.

nextGame.headline: Ankle decides it; Browns' pass defense is his first real test.
nextGame.body:
Cleveland is the first competent defense he would face, and it is built to stop what he has done best. The Browns rank 4th in pass EPA allowed and 5th in sack rate. They are also 3rd-stingiest against tight ends, which matters because Andrews is his most-targeted receiver. The weakness is on the ground: 29th in rush EPA allowed and last in explosive runs allowed. Offenses have run against them more than usual (passRateOverNorm -3.6). In a game with a 40.5 total, that points to a Henry-heavy, low-volume script rather than a big passing day. WR2s have found room (0.75 EPA per play, 30th), so Bateman is the likelier beneficiary than Andrews.

Availability is the story on both sides. Jackson is Out as of the latest report with a return date of game day, and center Cam Jurgens is in the final stages of concussion protocol. Losing his center would test protection that has been the second-best in the league at preventing hits. Cleveland is shorthanded inside: defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. are out, Kalia Davis is on IR, and linebacker Carson Schwesinger is questionable with an ankle sprain. That thins the interior that has to contain both Henry and a quarterback who may not be fully mobile. The forecast (12 mph wind, 18 mph gusts, more than three days out) is worth monitoring but is below the level that usually bends a passing game.

keyMatchups.title: Browns pass rush vs his clock
keyMatchups.body: He holds the ball 3.11 seconds and converts pressure into sacks at a middling rate, and Cleveland gets home on 8.2% of dropbacks. With a possible backup center and no proof he can escape on a bad ankle, this is where his efficiency is most at risk.

keyMatchups.title: Ravens run game vs thin interior
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland ranks 29th against the run and last in explosive runs allowed while missing two rotation defensive tackles. Baltimore already leans run-heavy, so expect volume to tilt to the ground and his passing attempts to stay modest.

keyMatchups.title: Andrews against a TE-stingy defense
keyMatchups.body: Tight ends are drawing an above-league share of targets against Cleveland but producing negative EPA (-0.19 a play, 3rd-best). If Andrews is muted, the passing game leans on Flowers and Bateman outside.

nextGame.watch: Whether he practices fully by Friday. If he plays, watch whether he scrambles, which tells you if the ankle is limiting him.

restOfSeason.body:
When healthy, the foundation is real: excellent protection, an aggressive downfield profile, and a receiver in Flowers who wins vertically. The 10-plus yards per attempt and +8 CPOE will regress as the schedule stiffens. His best seasons topped out near 8.8 yards per attempt, and that is a better anchor than this four-game sample. Passing volume will stay capped by a run-first offense that sits 27th in pass rate over expectation.

The rushing component is the bigger unknown. It was already trending down in 2025, and a sprained ankle could keep his designed runs near zero and blunt his scrambling for weeks. Expect strong efficiency and modest volume, with fantasy value leaning more on passing touchdowns than it did in his peak rushing years.
swingFactors: How quickly the ankle allows him to scramble again
Schedule shift from bottom-tier defenses to real ones

confidence.note: 96 attempts, all against bottom-eight defenses, plus an unresolved ankle sprain.
